sentences.text: A few exemptions to finish, and they’re worth easy points.
A vessel under seven meters at anchor doesn’t need an anchor light or shape, as long as she’s not in or near a narrow channel, a fairway, an anchorage, or anywhere other vessels normally navigate.
A vessel under twelve meters aground doesn’t need the aground lights or shapes.
And an Inland one: a vessel under twenty meters at anchor in a special anchorage area designated by the Coast Guard doesn’t need an anchor light or shape.
You’ll find those areas marked on the chart.
A seaplane or wing-in-ground craft that can’t show lights and shapes exactly as required shows them as closely as she can.
That’s lesson twelve, and it finishes the lights.
Red over red: not under command.
Pass a dredge on the green side.
One white light or one ball: at anchor.
Next time, we stop looking and start listening: sound signals.
